Repo: /home/user/fortress (Sun's Fortress language, 2012 Java/Scala codebase). Map the RUNTIME BYTECODE MACHINERY for an architecture explainer. Search breadth: very thorough. Report with file:line references throughout.

Questions to answer:
1. `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/InstantiatingClassloader.java` — how does it work end to end? How does it intercept class loading, how does it detect a "template" class name vs a normal one, what rewrites does it perform (walk its findClass/loadClass path and the ASM visitors it applies: MethodInstantiater, Instantiater, InstantiationMap). What classes does it SYNTHESIZE from nothing (tuples, arrows, unions — look for names like makeArrow, makeTuple, closure classes)? What is the Naming class's mangling scheme (the special characters/escapes it uses in class names to encode type parameters)?
2. Where do the "template" class files come from — i.e. in the compiler (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/`, esp. CodeGen.java), where are generic declarations emitted as templates with placeholder names? Where are compiled classes cached on disk (ByteCodeWriter, default_repository paths)?
3. `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/asmbytecodeoptimizer/` — what is this package? Who invokes ByteCodeOptimizer.java and when (is it on by default? find its call sites and any flags/properties gating it). What do the individual optimizations do (Inlining.java, RemoveLiteralCoercions.java, GenerateUnboxedVersions.java, AbstractInterpretation*.java)? Note it has its own Opcodes.java that shadows org.objectweb.asm.Opcodes.
4. Class file version: where is V1_6 (or version 50 / 0x32) set in codegen and in the rewriting path? Are stack map frames ever emitted or computed (COMPUTE_FRAMES / COMPUTE_MAXS usage across codegen and runtimeSystem)?
5. Any in-repo design documentation for this machinery: look for docs/, notes, README files near these packages, long explanatory comments at the top of key files, and anything under ProjectFortress/doc* or SpecData or DesignNotes mentioning codegen/generics/bytecode.

Return a structured report: (a) pipeline diagram in text from .fss source → compiled template .class in cache → runtime instantiation → JVM-loaded class; (b) per-package findings with file:line cites; (c) verbatim quotes of the most illuminating comments; (d) list of surprises/gotchas.

## The two worlds

The tree contains two nearly-disjoint executions of Fortress, and most
confusion comes from mixing them up:

| | interpreter ("walk") | bytecode compiler |
|---|---|---|
| era | 2003-lineage, mature | 2010–2012, the team's final push, incomplete |
| entry | `fortress <file>.fss` | `fortress compile <file>.fss` + `fortress run <component>` |
| libraries | `Library/` + `LibraryBuiltin/` (FortressBuiltin, NativeArray, ...) | `CompilerBuiltin`, `CompilerLibrary`, `CompilerAlgebra`, `CompilerSystem`, `GeneratorLibrary` |
| native mechanism | `builtinPrimitive("com.sun...glue.prim.X")` in .fss | `import java com.sun...nativeHelpers.{...}` in .fss |
| native String type | glue-level FString | `CompilerBuiltin.JavaString` / `StringVector` (foreign map in `NamingCzar`) |
| tests | `ProjectFortress/tests/` via `ant testSystem` | `compiler_tests/`, `library_tests/` via `ant testFast` etc. |

The mode switch is `com.sun.fortress.compiler.WellKnownNames`:
`useInterpreterLibraries()` / `useCompilerLibraries()` swap the meaning of
"the builtin library" (`FortressBuiltin` vs `CompilerBuiltin`) and "the
standard library" (`FortressLibrary` vs `CompilerLibrary`). `Shell.subMain`
calls one or the other per subcommand (`walk` vs `compile`/`run`/`link`).

Consequences:
- A `.fss` file is generally written for ONE world. `import java ...` means

The central idea: **the compiler never emits a class for an instantiated generic.** It emits a *template* whose name contains empty `⟦⟧` brackets, plus a sidecar `.xlation` metadata file. At runtime the reference site does a `GETSTATIC`/`NEW` against a class name that *does not exist on disk* — a mangled name encoding the full instantiation. `InstantiatingClassloader` intercepts the resulting load, parses the name back apart, finds the template, and rewrites it. Generics are reified lazily, per instantiation, by the classloader.

### 3. The ASM visitors

**`Instantiater.java`** (182 lines, `ClassVisitor`, ASM9 at `:36`). Holds two `InstantiationMap`s — `types` and `oprs` (`:29-30`). Rewrites the class name, superclass and every interface through `types.getTypeName` (`:47-61`); note `:53-55` carries a verbatim example of a fully-mangled real name as a comment. `visitField` (`:80-97`) has a subtlety: when a closure field's descriptor differs wrapped vs flattened, it emits **two** fields.

`visitMethod` (`:105-165`) is where tuple-flattening bridges are synthesized. When substitution turns a single generic parameter into a `Tuple`, and the class is not an interface and the method not static, it generates an *additional* method taking the tuple components un-flattened, which boxes them via `ConcreteTuple….make` and forwards (`:145-155`). Returns a `MethodInstantiater` wrapping the delegate (`:164`).

**`MethodInstantiater.java`** (297 lines, ASM9 at `:36`). Rewrites owners/names/descriptors on every instruction. Two notable behaviors:

- `visitFieldInsn` `:65-89`: on `PUTSTATIC` of a closure field whose wrapped and unwrapped descriptors differ, it expands one store into store/load/store to initialize both fields. Comment `:76-79`: *"This is a hack; when a closure looks different depending on how its descriptor translates (wrapped vs not), that means that there will be a second closure field, and it needs to be initialized."*
- `rttiReference` `:94-140`: recursively converts a *static* reference to an RTTI singleton into a *dynamic* chain of `INVOKESTATIC factory` calls — because the RTTI object for `List⟦ZZ32⟧` must be built at runtime from the RTTI for `ZZ32`. Special-cases tuples/arrows to `Tuple*N`/`Arrow*N`, and splits operator parameters out of type parameters using `xldata.isOprKind()`.

**`InstantiationMap.java`** (567 lines). Substitution engine. Every entry point (`getName` `:44`, `getTypeName` `:57`, `getFieldDesc` `:89`, `getMethodDesc` `:115`) first *demangles*, then walks with `maybeBareVar`/`maybeVarInTypeDesc`/`maybeVarInMethodSig`. **`ManglingClassWriter.java`** — since the ASM 9 upgrade this is a `ClassVisitor` delegating to an inner `ClassWriter`, per the comment at `:23-27`:

> `Under ASM 3 this class subclassed ClassWriter directly and overrode its`
> `visit methods to mangle names on the way in.  ASM 4+ makes every`
> `ClassWriter.visit* method final, so the mangling now lives in a`
> `ClassVisitor that delegates to an internal ClassWriter; only`
> `getCommonSuperClass still needs a ClassWriter subclass.`

`getCommonSuperClass` (`:38-57`) is required by `COMPUTE_FRAMES` and cannot fail, so it catches everything and returns `java/lang/Object`:

> `This returns java.lang.Object as the CommonSuperClass of anything involving an interface`
> `type.  Since all Fortress traits correspond to interface types, we ought to be able to`
> `do the same.`
> `That said, it still feels wrong.`

## (d) Surprises and gotchas

1. **The optimizer package is entirely dead.** Never called from the compiler; only reachable via `bin/BytecodeOptimize`. `ByteCodeOptimizer` isn't even `public`. Two of its six enabled passes (`AddString`, `CalculateLabels`) aren't optimizations, and the seventh (`GenerateUnboxedVersions`) is commented out *and* unimplemented — it only prints.

2. **`Opcodes` shadowing is invisible at the call site.** `import org.objectweb.asm.*` is silently defeated by the same-package `Opcodes` class. Values coincide today; a divergence would be a very quiet miscompile.

3. **Class names are load-bearing data structures.** The full instantiation — type args, operator args, arrow schema, self-index, closure marker — is encoded in the *class name string*. The classloader is a parser. There is no side table at load time beyond the `.xlation` sidecar.

4. **Class name ≠ file name, on purpose.** A template's file is `Stem⟦⟧…` while its internal `this_class` is `Stem⟦T,U⟧…`. `javap`-ing a cached template shows a class whose name doesn't match its path — this is intended, not corruption.

5. **`.xlation` sidecars live inside the jar next to `.class`.** They are found by `getResourceAsStream` on the same base name, which is why `bytecode_cache/*` must be on the classpath. Stale sidecars produce a `VersionMismatch` whose only remedy is deleting the cache.

6. **Only one classloader may ever exist** — enforced by a global system property and a hard `Error` (`:119-125`). The private constructor also throws.

7. **`loadClass` is overridden, not `findClass`** — inverting normal delegation. The allow-list in `ClassLoadChecker` (`:2890-2910`) is hand-maintained; a runtime class that must be shared but isn't listed gets loaded twice with confusing `ClassCastException`s.

8. **Union types trigger reflection during class loading** — `instantiateUnion` calls `icl.loadClass` on member types, intersects their transitive interfaces, and synthesizes forwarders. Class loading that recursively loads classes to decide what to emit.

9. **`AnyConcreteTuple.get(int)` uses a generated binary-search tree**, not a `tableswitch` (`visitBinaryTree` `:1799-1820`).

10. **Frames are never authored, always computed** — so every `visitMaxs` argument in the codebase is a lie, formalized as `Naming.ignoredMaxsParameter = 1`.

11. **`getCommonSuperClass` cannot fail**, so it swallows all `Throwable` and returns `Object`. Combined with `COMPUTE_FRAMES` this means frame computation quietly widens types rather than erroring — the author's own "it still feels wrong."

12. **`Instantiater` can emit methods that were never in the template** — the tuple-flattening bridge at `:129-160` appears only when substitution happens to produce a `Tuple`. The instantiated class can have a different method count than its template.

13. **A live tripwire in `mangleFortressIdentifier`**: `if (t.contains("\\|FVoid")) throw new Error("AHA!")` (`Naming.java:695-696`) — a debugging assertion left in shipping code.

14. **`SNOWMAN` (☃) doubles as the void/empty-tuple type**, and arity-1-with-void must be special-cased to arity 0 in several places (`:1004`, `:1222`, `closureClassPrefix` comments `:669-677`).

15. **Compile-time and load-time agree only by convention** — `Naming.makeTemplateSParams` (returns `⟦⟧`) and `InstantiationMap.canonicalizeStaticParameters` (strips to `⟦⟧`) are separate functions in separate packages with no shared constant and no test tying them together. Change either and every generic silently fails to resolve.
